thread.title: After the Bell: Dow Jumps 108 Points to Make July Best Month Since January

author: Ben Levisohn
title: After the Bell: Dow Jumps 108 Points to Make July Best Month Since January
text:
By Ben Levisohn July 31, 2018 6:14 p.m. ET Finishing Strong. The Dow ended July on an upbeat note as potential talks with China on trade gave the market a boost . Apple reported earnings after Tuesday's close and proved some tech stocks still got it. What the Federal Reserve says on Wednesday could go a long way in determining whether stocks will start off August on the right track. In today's After the Bell , we...
Illustration: Scott Olson/Getty Images •...explain why tech might underperform in the weeks ahead;
•...review Illumina's (ILMN) earnings;
•...and highlight IPG Photonics (IPGP) drop to the bottom of the S&P 500.
All Months Should Be This Easy It was a good end to a great month.
The S&P 500 gained 3.6% in July after rising 0.5% to 2816.29 today. The Dow climbed 4.7% this month after advancing 108.36 points, or 0.4%, to 25,415.19 today. The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.2% this month after gaining 0.6% to 7671.79 today. It was the best month for each index since January.
Today may have marked the end of the brutal rotation out of what had been working that occurred after Facebook (FB) disappointed investors last week , as the Nasdaq broke a three-day losing streak. Facebook actually rose today, as did Twitter (TWTR)–another victim of earnings–and Apple 's (AAPL) better-than-expected earnings has that stock trading up nearly 3% after Tuesday's close.
But make no mistake. There's a good chance that tech will continue to lag in the days and weeks ahead, says UBS strategist Keith Parker . It's not because there's anything wrong with tech. It offers sales and earnings growth that's nearly double the S&P 500's buybacks that are increasing at a rapid rate. Yet too many investors already own these stocks–Parker puts growth funds have positions at 1.4 standard deviations above average–and that could "prolong the rotation," he says. "Within value, Financials/Banks still look tactically attractive to us while Industrials remains our preferred cyclical catch up trade."
But we're always tempted to look for the touch of gray in any silver lining, and we found one courtesy of Gavekal Research's Louis Gave . In a note release today, he wonders whether the stocks market deserves a greater risk premium—i.e., a lower P/E—if "one of the world’s top five stocks by market cap can see a fifth of its value erased in just 24 hours." It could be overseas investors, who have put large amounts of money into U.S. markets in recent year, who have the answer to that question. "Foreign capital inflows into the U.S. in recent years have been fairly consistent, predicated in large part on the premise that U.S. markets offered more stability, better liquidity and higher returns than markets elsewhere in the world," Gave writes. "But if valuations in the tech sector have now been pushed too high, and if the risk profile of U.S. large-cap stocks turns out to be less attractive than most have assumed, then we will clearly be entering a new phase in the market."
I thought we already had?
The Hot Stock Illumina (ILMN) shot to the top of the S&P 500 today after it posted better-than-expected second-quarter earnings.
The DNA-sequencing firm was up $35.12, or 12.1%, to $324.36.
Illumina’s revenue jumped 25% to $830 million compared to $662 million in the same period last year. “The recently launched platform NovaSeq system exceeded investor expectations,” says Michael Waterhouse , an analyst at Morningstar . “Along with its other product lines, we continue to forecast long-term double-digit revenue growth.”
Shares of Illumina is up 48.5% year to date and 63.9% for the past year. — Varada Bhat
The S&P 500’s Top 5 Stocks:
Illumina (ILMN): 12.1%
KLA-Tencor (KLAC): 10.5%
Harris Corp (HRS): 9.7%
Xylem (XYL): 9.3%
Aptiv (APTV): 6%
The Biggest Loser IPG Photonics (IPGP) lost a quarter of its value after it missed revenue estimates , making the maker of fiber lasers the worst performer in the S&P 500 index.
The shares were down 26.9%, or $60.26, to $164.04.
Despite the growth in orders on a year-over-year basis, the company failed to meet its target as demand softened in Europe and China at the end of the quarter.“IPG Photonics confirmed what many had feared," says Longbow Research analyst Joe Wittine . "The geopolitical factors caused some pause in investment for their metal fabrication in China and Europe.” The company lowered its full-year guidance with concerns of trade tensions hurting growth overseas.
S hares of IPG Photonics were down 23.4% year to date but were slightly up 1.1% for the past year. — V.B.
